title: Regulation on Financing Business
text:
Unofficial English Translation
REGULATION ON FINANCING BUSINESS
Regulation number: 2021/R-132
(translation)
(Effective 17th October 2021)

REGULATION ON FINANCING BUSINESS
CHAPTER ONE
PRELIMINARY
Introduction and (a)
1. This Regulation is issued to provide for licensing,
title
regulating and supervision of Financing Businesses,
and other matters thereof.
(b) This Regulation is issued under Section 29 and 38 of
the Maldives Monetary Authority Act 1981 (Law no.
6/81).
(c) This Regulation shall be cited as “Regulation on
Financing Business.”
Commencement
2. This Regulation shall come into effect from the date of
publication in the Government Gazette.
CHAPTER TWO
ISSUANCE, SUSPENSION, AND REVOCATION OF LICENCE
Prohibitions to (a)
3. No person shall carry on, purport to show they carry on,
persons without
or advertise Financing Business in the Maldives without
Licence
a Licence issued by the Authority for the provision of
Financing Business.
(b) In carrying out a business or providing a service, except
with the approval of the Authority, no person except for
Licensees, may use as part of its name, whether in
Dhivehi or any other language, the following phrases or
words; or phrases or words associated with the
following phrases or words; or any phrases or words
2

that may indicate the person is conducting Financing
Business:
(1)
“financing company” or “financing”
(2)
“finance leasing company” or “finance leasing” or
“leasing” or “leasing finance”
Exempted
4. Notwithstanding any other section of this Regulation, this
Institutions
Regulation shall not be applicable to banks and insurance
companies licensed by the Authority.
Applications for (a)
5. An application for license shall be made in writing to the
Licence
Authority in accordance with this Regulation.
(b) The following information and documents shall be
submitted along with an application for Licence:
(1) copies of the proposed Memorandum of
Association and the Articles of Association of the
proposed company;
(2) the proposed Capital funds and the sources of
such funds; the Capital funds must be free from
any encumbrance or impairment. If the Authority
so requires, the applicant shall submit a
certificate, in such form as required by the
Authority, stating that there is no encumbrance
on the funds.
(3) the name of the proposed business;
(4) the names, nationality, permanent address,
income source, and other additional information
stipulated by the Authority, of Major
Shareholders, Ultimate Beneficial Owners, board
of directors, and Senior Management of the
proposed company;
3

(5) the financial statements of the preceding 3
(three) years of the proposed company’s Major
Shareholders that are legal entities; current
financial statements of the proposed company’s
Major Shareholders who are natural persons; and
current financial statements of the proposed
company’s Ultimate Beneficial Owners. The
financial statements of legal entities shall show
the entity’s financial information as well the
consolidated financial information of any group
to which the entity belongs, and shall be audited.
The Authority may also require that financial
statements of natural persons to be audited;
(6) for each Major Shareholder, Ultimate Beneficial
Owner, director of board and Senior
Management member of the proposed company,
a police clearance record and an affidavit duly
signed by the person stating any convictions for
crimes or no conviction, involvement as a board
member or Senior Management member in an
insolvent company or a company subject to
insolvency proceedings, if any;
(7) list of all entities in which any proposed Major
Shareholder or Ultimate Beneficial Owner holds
any interests, specifying the size of such
interests and the registered addresses of such
entities;
(8) A business plan describing the intended manner
of operating the proposed business, including:
(i) a description of its organisational structure,
corporate governance and risk
management frameworks and internal
controls;
4

(ii) measures appropriate to counter money-
laundering and the financing of terrorism;
and
(iii) projected financial statements with realistic
assumptions including balance sheets
profit and loss statements, and cash flow
statements, for the first 3 (three) years of
operations.
(c) The applicant shall provide additional documents
requested by the Authority for clarification purposes in
the course of the licensing process.
(d) The Authority may require the Capital funds be
deposited at the Authority or at a bank determined by
the Authority.
(e) Applicant shall provide without delay the information
and documents required when submitting the
application, as well as other information requested by
the Authority for the purposes of processing the
application. In the event that the applicant fails to
provide all the information and documents necessary
within 3 (three) months from the date of applying for
Licence, or fails to provide additional documents
requested under paragraph (c) within the timeframe
stipulated by the Authority, the Authority may deem the
application to have been abandoned and the application
fee forfeited.
Application Fee for
6. An application for Licence shall be accompanied by the
Licence
amount stated in Regulation No.: 2016/R-80 (Regulation on
Fees and Charges Payable by Financial Institutions) as the
application fee for financing business. The application fee is
non-refundable whether the Authority grants or refuses the
Licence.
5

General (a)
7. Licence shall only be granted once the applicant
preconditions for
registers the company under Law no. 10/96
issuing a Licence
(Companies Act of Maldives).
(b)
Licence shall only be granted to conduct business
activities at an office established in the Maldives.
Granting or (a)
8. Authority may decide either of the following in relation
refusing Licence
to an application for a Licence:
(1) grant the Licence, with or without imposing
conditions, obligations, or restrictions to such
Licence as determined by the Authority; or
(2) refuse to grant the Licence.
(b) In granting a Licence, the Authority will specify the
whether the Licence is Tier 1 or Tier 2 financing
company, and the type of Financing Business or
Financing Business activities allowed.
Change to the
9. Where such an application is made by the Licensee, the
Licence
Authority may remove a financial business activity which the
Authority has approved for the Licensee when the licence was
issued. Similarly, the Authority may also add an activity to the
financial business activities upon a similar application by the
Licensee.
Licensing (a)
10. The Authority may impose licensing conditions in
Conditions
addition to those stated in paragraph (b) when granting
a Licence. The Authority may also impose additional
licensing conditions subsequent to the initial licensing,
and modify or waive any conditions of licensing in
writing.
6

(b) Licensees shall always act in accordance with the
following conditions:
(1) commence the business operations within 12
(twelve) months of granting the Licence, unless a
shorter period is provided to start the business
as a condition of the Licence;
(2) comply with all Capital requirements, prudential
requirements and any other requirements
determined by the Authority;
(3) establish appropriate systems and implement
policies to manage risk to their operations and
business, including appropriate corporate
governance and risk management frameworks,
and policies for internal controls and audit;
(4) conduct business in accordance with the
business plan submitted to the Authority with the
Licence application, and not deviate with or
revise the business plan unless with the prior
approval of the Authority;
(5) conduct business in a prudent manner and in
accordance with laws, and regulations and
directives issued by the Authority;
(6) not engage in or facilitate in any way, in criminal
activities including criminal breach of trust, fraud,
money laundering and financing of terrorism;
(7) conduct the business only under the name that
has been approved by the Authority;
7

(8) ensure that all Major Shareholders, members of
the board of directors and Senior Management
members of the Licensee are at all times fit and
proper in accordance with the standards
determined by the Authority;
(9) not engage in any business other than the
Licensed business without obtaining approval
from the Authority.
Suspension and The Authority may suspend or revoke the Licence where
11.
Revocation of the Authority believes that one of the following events
Licence or circumstances has occurred:
(a) Licensee has knowingly submitted any
misleading or false information with its
application for the Licence;
(b) Licensee has failed to comply with any law, or
any regulation or order or directive issued by the
Authority, or any condition of the licence;
(c) Licensee has informed that its business is not
viable or has ceased or decided to cease its
business;
(d) Licensee is carrying out its business activities in
a manner that the Authority considers is unsafe
and unsound;
(e) Licensee becomes insolvent, or is wound up or
otherwise dissolved;
(f) Licensee has not submitted any information,
document or report requested by the Authority;
8

(g) any major shareholder, Ultimate Beneficial
Owner, member of the board of directors, or
member of Senior Management is not fit and
proper;
(h) Licensee has misled the Authority or provided
false or misleading information to the Authority.
Annual Fee (a)
12. Licensees shall pay the amount prescribed in
Regulation No.: 2016/R-80 (Regulation on Fees and
Charges Payable by Financial Institutions) as the annual
fee for financing companies.
(b) The annual fee paid by the Licensees under this section
is non-refundable even if the Licence is revoked,
suspended, or the Licensee has ceased the operation of
business.
CHAPTER THREE
PRUDENTIAL REQUIREMENTS AND SUPERVISION OF FINANCING COMPANIES
Capital (a)
13. All Tier 1 Financing Business Licensees shall, at all
requirements
times, maintain an amount not less than 50,000,000/-
applicable to
(fifty million) Rufiyaa as minimum unimpaired Capital.
Licensees
The Capital funds cannot be borrowed money and must
be free from any encumbrance.
(b) All Tier 2 Financing Business Licensees shall, at all
times, maintain an amount not less than 20,000,000/-
(twenty million) Rufiyaa as minimum unimpaired
Capital. The Capital funds cannot be borrowed money
and must be free from any encumbrance.
(c) Licensees shall maintain at all times:
9

(1) a Capital adequacy ratio not less than 12%
(twelve percent), and
(2) a leverage ratio not less than 10% (ten percent).
(d) The Authority shall inform Licensees the manner of
calculating the Capital adequacy ratio and leverage
ratio, as well as the types of assets and Capital to be
considered.
Minimum required (a)
14. Licensees shall establish and maintain a minimum
Capital reserve
required Capital reserve which is not less than the
Licensee’s Capital amount stipulated in Section 13 (a)
and (b) of this Regulation. This reserve shall be
accumulated as follows:
(1) allocate, after taxes, at least 50% (fifty percent)
of its net, distributable profits for the formation
of the minimum required Capital reserve until the
reserve totals 50% (fifty percent) of its minimum
required Capital; and
(2) once the reserve reaches 50% (fifty percent) of
the Licensee’s minimum required Capital,
allocate after taxes, not less than 25% (twenty
five percent) of the Licensee’s net, distributable
profit until the reserve totals an amount equal to
the Licensee’s minimum required Capital.
Provisioning
15. Licensees shall make adequate provisions for credit loss,
depreciation of assets, and other losses, in accordance with
any guidelines issued by the Authority or international
accounting standards, whichever is more stringent.
Exposure Limits (a)
16. The following amounts shall be the maximum Exposure
limits that can be maintained by Licensees:
10

(1) the total Exposure outstanding at any time,
including both funded and unfunded Exposure, to
a single person, or to a group of closely-related
persons treated as a single person, shall not at
any time exceed 15% (fifteen percent) of the
Licensee’s Capital base. This total Exposure to a
single person, or to a group of closely-related
persons treated as a single person, may be
increased up to 30% (thirty percent) of the
Licensee’s Capital base under certain exceptions
for low risk lending, in accordance with
guidelines issued by the Authority.
(2) the total Exposure, funded and unfunded,
outstanding at any time to a borrowing group
shall not exceed 40% (forty percent) of the
Licensee's Capital base provided that:
(i)
no one member of the borrowing group
shall exceed 15% (fifteen percent) of the
Licensee’s Capital base;
(ii)
each member of the borrowing group shall
have the capacity to repay their stand-alone
Exposure from their normal operations;
(iii)
the security pledged for stand-alone
Exposure by each member of the borrowing
group shall be separate from other
members;
(iv)
the money or profit/advantage? received
from a stand-alone Exposure by each
member of the borrowing group shall only
be utilised by the member who
borrowed/borrowing member?
(3) the total of all large Exposures shall not at any
time exceed 500% (five hundred percent) of the
Licensee’s Capital base.
11

(4) The Exposure for each related person or related
corporate group shall not exceed 15% (fifteen
percent) of the Licensee’s Capital base. And, the
total of all Exposures for all related persons or
related corporate group shall be up to a
maximum of 50 % (fifty percent) of the Licensee’s
Capital base.
(b) Any direct Exposure to the Government, or an Exposure
which the Government has unconditionally guaranteed
as to payment of principal and interest or profit payable,
shall be exempted from the limits specified in (a).
(c) For the purposes of this section, authority will inform the
definition of “Capital Base,” “Large Exposure,”
“Borrowing Group,” “Related Persons” to the Licensees.
Restriction on
17. Licensees shall not accept their own shares as security for any
loans secured by
Exposure. However, Licensees may take their own shares as
own shares and
security to avoid a loss on an Exposure granted previously,
reacquisition of
with the prior approval of the Authority and under such
shares
conditions imposed by the Authority. Licensees shall also not
buy back any of their shares without prior approval of the
Authority. Licensee’s own shares held, and Exposures secured
by shares of Licensees shall be deducted from Capital for
purposes of calculating minimum Capital and Capital
adequacy ratios.
Prohibition on (a)
18. A Tier 1 Financing Business Licensee shall not accept
accepting deposit
deposits, except term deposits of more than 1 (one) year
from legal persons with the permission of the Authority.
(b)
A Tier 2 Financing Business Licensee shall not accept
any deposits from any party.
Prohibited
19. Licensee shall not carry-out or participate in carrying-out with
activities
another person, any business activity such as wholesaling,
retailing, manufacturing, transportation business, agriculture,
12

fisheries, tourism, mining, construction, and insurance
underwriting. Licensees shall also not act as an agent for or a
partner of another person, except as an agent of an insurance
business with the permission of the Authority.
Permissible (a)
20. Licensees may not invest in any business or company
Investments
except as provided in this section. Notwithstanding the
foregoing, Licensees providing services in accordance
with Shari’ah principles may, provide finance in
accordance with the requirements prescribed by the
Authority.
(b) Licensees shall not invest in the stocks, bonds, shares
or equity-linked bonds of any company in an amount
that exceeds 15% (fifteen percent) of the Licensee’s
Capital. Such investments, except for the case where a
company is a financial institution, shall not exceed 5%
(five percent) of the voting interest of the company.
(c) Licensees shall not acquire more than 5 % (five percent)
of the voting shares of a financial institution without the
prior approval of the Authority. The Authority may grant
such approval with or without stipulating conditions.
(d) Licensees shall not acquire real estate or retain legal
title of real estate except for the purposes stated below:
(1) to accommodate their own business operations
and to provide housing for employees;
(2) to acquire real estate required to provide Shari’ah
compliant services, in accordance with any
regulations issued or instructions provided by
the Authority; and
(3) to hold real estate temporarily during the course
of realising on collateral for loans.
13

(e) Licensees shall dispose of any investment made
against any ownership interests in companies or
financial institutions in excess of the limitations
provided in this section acquired in the course of their
Financing Business, within 6 (six) months after such
interest were acquired, unless the Authority, for good
cause shown, extends the permitted holding period for
an additional time not exceeding 6 (six) additional
months. Any interest in real estate acquired in the
course of business operations, under paragraph (d)(3)
of this section shall be disposed of within 2 (two) years
after such interests were acquired, unless the Authority,
for good cause shown, extends the permitted holding
period for an additional period not exceeding 2 (two)
years.
Minimum Licensees shall maintain adequate liquid assets
21.
requirement of capable of settling the Licensee’s liabilities when due,
Liquid Assets and in accordance with any limit determined by the
Authority. In setting such limits, the types of assets
which shall be considered liquid assets, as well as the
manner of calculating the liquid asset requirement shall
be informed by the Authority
Establishing a (a)
22. Licensees shall not establish an office or a branch or a
subsidiary and
subsidiary either in the Maldives or abroad, without the
office and
approval of the Authority. Licensees shall also not
appointing agents
provide a service relating to the Licensed business
through any agent without the approval of the Authority.
(b) Licensees shall provide 60 (sixty) days’ prior notice to its
customers and the Authority of the closing of an office
or branch or subsidiary, and shall provide to the
Authority a detailed plan for termination of business in
such office, branch or subsidiary.
Change in (a)
23. Where any person, acting directly or indirectly or
ownership and
through another person, plans to acquire shares to a
becoming a Major
limit that would make such person a Major Shareholder
Shareholder
or an Ultimate Beneficial Owner, the person shall obtain
the approval of the Authority before acquiring the
14

shares. A person shall be deemed to be acquiring shares
through another person or persons, if the Authority is of
the view that that such persons are jointly trying to
acquire the Licensee’s voting shares pursuant to an
agreement, whether formal or informal.
(b) Any request for approval under paragraph (a), shall be
accompanied with the following information:
(1) the name, nationality, permanent address, and
the business or profession of the proposed Major
Shareholder and the Ultimate Beneficial Owner of
the proposed Major Shareholder where
applicable, and the personal financial statements
which shall be audited statements if the
Authority so requires; and any other information
of the shareholder and the Ultimate Beneficial
Owners as may be stipulated by the Authority.
(2) where the proposed Major Shareholder is a legal
entity, information stipulated under paragraph
(b)(1) on the legal entity and its Ultimate
Beneficial Owners; and the audited financial
statements of the legal entity for the preceding 3
(three) years. The financial statements of legal
entities shall show both the financial information
of the legal entity, and consolidated financial
information of the group to which the legal entity
belongs, if applicable.
(3) for each proposed Major Shareholder or Ultimate
Beneficial Owner, a police clearance record and
an affidavit duly signed by the person stating any
convictions for crimes or no conviction past or
present, involvement as a member of the board
or Senior Management in an insolvent company
or a company subject to insolvency proceedings;
15

(4) a list of other entities in which the proposed
Major Shareholder and Ultimate Beneficial
Owners hold interests, specifying the size of such
interests and the registered addresses of the
entities;
(5) the terms and conditions of the proposed
acquisition, as well as the manner in which the
acquisition is to be made;
(6) the source and amount of the funds to be used in
the acquisition;
(7) where a major change is intended to be brought
to the Licensee’s business, corporate structure,
or management, details of such change; and
(8) any other information required by the Authority.
(c) Any Major Shareholder, acting directly or indirectly or in
concert with other persons, who proposes to increase
an existing holding in a Licensee in a manner that would
reach or exceed a threshold of 20% (twenty percent), or
33% (thirty three percent) or 50% (fifty percent),of the
Licensee’s Capital or the voting rights, shall obtain the
approval of the Authority prior to acquiring the
additional shares. For any such request, the Authority
may require the submission of any or all of the
information in paragraph (b) of this section.
(d) Licensees shall promptly notify the Authority upon
becoming aware of a proposed acquisition of their
shares as stipulated in paragraph (a) and (c) of this
section.
16

Merger of a Licensees shall not merge or consolidate with another
24.
financing company financing company except with the prior approval of the
with another Authority. The Authority may refuse approval for such
financing company requests.
Accounting (a)
25. Licensees shall maintain books, financial statements,
Principles and
records and documents as may be reasonable to ensure
Maintenance of
the orderly operations of their business. Licensees shall
Records
ensure that the following records and documents are
maintained:
(1) Customer identification records;
(2) Applications by customers and documents
pertaining to transactions, a signed record of the
decision of the Licensee approving the
transactions, and all documents or records
relating to suspicious transactions; and
(3) Any other records or documents stipulated by
the Authority.
(b) Unless otherwise stipulated by the Authority, Licensees
shall maintain all financial statements, records and
documents in the Maldives. And Licensees shall
maintain such financial statements, records and
documents in either Dhivehi or English Language.
(c) Unless otherwise stipulated by the Authority, Licensees
shall maintain records and documents collected
regarding business relationships for a period of 5 (five)
years from the termination of such business
relationships. This includes, but not limited to the
customer identification information, transaction history,
and any other information and documents related to the
respective business relationship.
17

(d) Unless otherwise stipulated by the Authority, Licensees
shall maintain all documents and records apart from
those stated in paragraph (c) for a minimum of 5 (five)
years.
(e) Licensees shall ensure the retention of all records that
are relevant to any on-going litigation, or records which
they reasonably determine may be required by an
investigative authority for an on-going criminal
investigation that the licensees are aware of, or any
records that they reasonably determine may be required
for a reasonably foreseeable litigation action. Such
records shall be retained despite the minimum record
retention period stipulated in paragraph (c) and (d), for
such time as the Licensees reasonably determine that
the records are no longer required for the purposes
above.
(f) Licensees shall apply accounting rules and systems in
conformity with international accounting standards,
including the use of full accrual accounting, and in
compliance with any special requirements of the
Authority in this regard, if any.
Financial Year
26. The financial year of Licensees shall commence on 1st
January and end on 31st December of the same year.
Financial (a)
27. Licensees shall prepare their financial statements:
Statements
including balance sheet, profit and loss statement,
annual cash flow statements, and statements of
changes in capital accounts, in a manner that gives a
true and fair view of their financial position.
(b) Licensees shall submit a copy of their audited financial
statements to the Authority, within 4 (four) months from
the end of every financial year. Where the auditor sends
a letter accompanying such audited financial
statements to the Licensee, a copy of such letter shall
also be submitted to the Authority along with the
audited financial statements.
18

Annual Report (a)
28. Licensees shall submit to the Authority, their annual
report, including any reports sent to the Licensee’s
directors and management to shareholders, within 30
(thirty) days after it becomes available, and no later than
4 (four) months after the end of the financial year.
(b) The annual report of Licensees shall contain such
information as may be prescribed by Authority,
including a report by the board of directors of the
Licensee’s business during the preceding year and
expected future developments.
Audit (a)
29. Licensees shall appoint an external auditor.. Licensee
shall ensure that the external auditor satisfies any
conditions stipulated by the Authority, if any.
(b) Licensees shall include the following terms in the
agreement for appointment of external auditor:
(1) All reports and working papers prepared by the
external auditor must, upon request, be made
available to the Authority.
(2) The external auditor shall, at the request of the
Authority, undertake such additional
assignments or prepare such additional reports
regarding the Licensee, as the Authority may
request.
(c) No Licensee shall appoint the same external audit firm
continuously for a period of more than 4 (four) years
without Authority’s permission.
(d) The Authority may designate the external auditor,
appointed by the Licensee pursuant to paragraph (a), to
19

conduct an audit or assessment of the business or a
specific operational activity of the Licensee, or to
inspect the Licensee’s compliance to laws, and
regulations and instructions of the Authority. Or the
Authority may appoint another external auditor for this
purpose.
(e) The cost for performing any such additional work
designated by Authority and the cost incurred in
appointing another external auditor under paragraph (d)
shall be borne by the Licensee.
Submission of (a)
30. Licensees shall submit to the Authority, information,
Information and
documents and reports at such time, and in such
reports, and
manner and with such details as the Authority may
supervision
specify.
(b) The Authority may at any time conduct an on-site
examination of a Licensee, through its officers or
persons appointed by the Authority, for the purpose of
determining the financial position of the Licensee,
capability of the management, policies prescribed by
the Board to prevent and manage risk, the extent to
which the Licensee complies with the applicable laws
and regulations, or any other matter that the Authority
deems necessary. The Authority reserves the right to
examine records, books, minutes of meetings, and other
documents; gather information; and copy documents of
the Licensee during such an on-site examination.
(c) A Licensee shall provide any additional information or
documentation or evidence required by officers of the
Authority during or in connection with an on-site
examination stated in paragraph (b), or submit such
information to the Authority in writing where so
requested. Where necessary, the Licensee shall
corroborate in writing to the Authority, the authenticity
of such information.
20

(d) Where a Licensee fails to submit information, records or
documents to the Authority under paragraph (a) or (c)
within the time period or date specified by the Authority,
the Authority may, as an administrative penalty, impose
a fine not exceeding 100,000 (one hundred thousand)
Rufiyaa per day of delay, and instruct the Licensee to
pay such fine to the Authority.
CHAPTER FOUR
ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS
Administrative (a)
31. The Authority may take one or more measures or
sanctions
impose one or more penalties set out in paragraph (b)
of Section 39 of Law No.: 6/81 (Maldives Monetary
Authority Act 1981) where the Authority determines or
has grounds to believe that a Licensee, or a member of
the board of directors or Senior Management of the
Licensee, or any other person associated with the
Licensee has or may:
(1) Violated or violate the provisions of this
Regulation or the Law No.:6/81 (Maldives
Monetary Authority Act 1981) or any regulation
issued under the Act; any conditions of licensing,
instruction, or order issued by the Authority; or
(2) conducted or conduct the business in a manner
that is unsafe or unsound.
(b) The Authority may impose an administrative penalty not
exceeding 100,000 (hundred thousand) Rufiyaa per day
on a Licensee in the following circumstances until the
circumstance has ceased or compliance is obtained:
(1) the Licensee’s submission to the Authority,
intentionally or negligently, any materially
deficient or false statements; information; or
data; or
21

submission of materially deficient information or
data or such information or data with false
statements to the Authority, either intentionally
or negligently; or
(2) failure to provide the Authority with any
information, document or report in its
possession that is requested by the Authority.
Transitional
32. All Financing Businesses already operating under a licence
provision for
issued by the Authority prior to the commencement of this
existing financing
Regulation, shall be deemed to be Licensed as a Tier 1
companies
Financing Business and shall be subjected to full compliance
of this Regulation. Unless otherwise stated by the Authority,
any existing non-compliance to this Regulation shall be
brought into compliance by such Licensees within a period not
exceeding 1 (one) year from the commencement of this
Regulation.
Exempting or (a)
33. The Authority may exempt the Licensee from complying
changing
with any section or sections in this Regulation, either
requirements
with or without conditions, upon such request for
applicable to
exemption by the Licensee.
Licensees
(b) The Authority reserves the right to revoke, at any time,
any exemption granted under paragraph (a) of this
section.
Definitions
34. In this Regulation, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) “Ultimate Beneficial Owner” means a natural person
who is either directly or indirectly, ultimately an effective
Major Shareholder of a legal entity.
(b) “Capital” means the aggregate of the company’s paid-up
capital and its reserves, deduction having been made for
any loss appearing in the accounts of the company. This
shall exclude such reserves as the Authority may
specify in writing.
22

(c) “Authority” means the Maldives Monetary Authority
established under Law No.: 6/81 (Maldives Monetary
Authority Act 1981).
(d) “Exposure” shall include:
(1) any sum of money agreed to be disbursed to a
person subject to repayment, and any
outstanding repayment of a sum of money
disbursed, and any interest, profit or service
charge to be paid in relation to such
disbursements;
(2) any finance lease agreed to be arranged for a
person, or any lease payments due from an
existing finance lease arrangement, and any
interest, profit, or service charges to be paid in

(e) “Major Shareholder” means a person who, directly or
indirectly, holds a minimum of 10% (ten percent) of the
Capital or the voting rights of a legal entity, or who
through other means, in the opinion of the Authority,
controls the legal entity.
(f) “Financing Business” means the business of lending
money or providing finance leasing to the public from
funds borrowed from public or any other funds. This

does not include the business of selling own goods on
credit or instalment basis. Furthermore, lending
activities carried out by the government and such
lending or providing finance leasing businesses carried
out by the councils are also exempted from this
business.
(g) “Licence” means the Licence issued by the Authority to
carry on a Financing Business.
(h) “Licensee” means any person licensed by the Authority
to conduct a Financing Business.
(i) “Senior Management” includes a person who is an
employee of the Licensee who, regardless of title,
participates in policymaking functions; or is responsible
for any material portion of the Licensee’s activities; or is
the head of investing, internal audit, risk, or compliance.
The chief executive officer, general manager, chief
credit or financing officer, and chief financial officer are
included in this definition.
